thread:
Priya (oncall): quick handoff — seeing a small but persistent p95 latency bump and a ~0.8% 429 tail on embedding requests in us-west-2 since ~19:10 UTC. small customer impact: a handful of sessions retried by clients. no full outage.

incident-bot: PAGE severity: P2 — High-latency tail causing customer retries. Triggers: embedding-p95 > 300ms for 5+ mins, 429-rate > 0.5% for 3+ mins.

oncall-bot: Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-tail (playbook: batching -> autoscaler -> degrade).

Jorge M.: oof. any correlating infra events? node flaps / gpu evictions?

Priya (oncall): checked nodes and kube events — no node flaps. eviction loop logs show increased KV cache purge activity at ~19:08. embedding autoscaler scaled up 2x at 19:09, but requests were already queuing and the batcher backlog spiked.

Samira: posting quick graphs — embedding-p95: 120ms baseline -> 410ms spike; batcher-queue-length: baseline 30 -> 420 at peak; pod_cpu: not saturated.

Kai: my guess — a mismatch between the batcher concurrency and autoscaler granularity. autoscaler reacts to CPU, but batcher queue grows from token-limited bundling; results in larger batches and higher p95 for short windows, plus backpressure returned as 429s when queue hits max.

Priya (oncall): agreed. Mitigation taken: reduced batch_max_wait from 40ms -> 20ms on service embedding-v2 (rolled to 25% canary at 19:18), reconfigured batcher_max_queue to 500 -> 1200 to avoid immediate drops, and applied short-term rate limit increase for internal retry window.

Jorge M.: where's the canary? link?

Priya (oncall): canary link: https://deploys.redwood/internal/rollouts/embedding-v2/2026-06-22-1918. Canary looked healthy at 19:22 with p95 down to 190ms. 429s stopped within 6m of the changes.

Samira: confirmed reduced 429-rate to 0.05% (from 0.8%). customer retry logs show success within 2 attempts. No customer-facing alert escalations so far.

incident-bot: Note: remember to run post-incident eval if we fully revert batcher settings. Tag: ops-affects-embeddings.

Kai: long-term action: autoscaler SLO needs a signal from queue length or batch-latency, not just CPU. Filed a ticket.

Priya (oncall): opened ticket and linked traces: https://redwood.internal/tickets/RED-4412 — title: "embedding autoscaler: integrate batcher backlog metric into scaling policy". Assigned: Kai. ETA: sprint+1.

Jorge M.: for the handoff: primary for next window (19:30-23:30 UTC): Jorge (primary). Secondary: Samira. Coverage notes: keep an eye on batcher-queue-length and embedding-p95. If p95 > 300ms for 5+ min, follow runbook: reduce batch_max_wait -> 15ms and temporarily scale up dedicated gen-pool by +10% (k8s annot -> autoscaler override).

Priya (oncall): I've captured the exact commands below (used for canary rollback/adjust):

```bash
# reduce batch_max_wait on configmap and trigger rolling restart
kubectl -n redwood set env deploy/embedding-v2 BATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS=20
kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/embedding-v2
# increase internal retry window
kubectl -n redwood patch configmap embedding-ratelimit --type merge -p '{"data":{"retry_window_s":"8"}}'
```

Samira: adding runbook pointer to the thread: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/embeddings-batcher (sections: quick-mitigations, metrics-to-watch, escalation). Also PR with longer-term autoscaler change: https://git.redwood/repo/ops/merge_requests/782.

Jorge M.: any customers to proactively message?

Priya (oncall): Slack DMed support with summary + small cohort list — they will flag any escalations. No high-touch customers impacted per initial scan.

Kai: monitoring alerts to watch: embedding-p95 (>300ms), batcher-queue-length (>300), embedding-429-rate (>0.5%). I've added a temporary composite alert to reduce noise while we monitor.

Priya (oncall): next steps for the oncoming shift: 1) keep an eye on the canary rollout for the next 45m; 2) if p95 creeps above 300ms for >5m, promote the safe config to 100% and notify infra to apply pool scale; 3) follow-up ticket for autoscaler metric.

Jorge M.: got it. I'll be primary. Samira is on standby. Priya, leaving you the final note — thanks for stabilizing.

Priya (oncall): leaving shift. logging final state: canary at 25% -> p95 180ms, 429 0.05%. customer impact low. tickets: RED-4412. handover complete. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded. Reminder: please run post-incident eval if you promote changes to prod longer than 2h.

Samira: I'll watch the dashboards for the first hour and ping if anything regresses. Good handoff.

Jorge M.: logging timeline note in #postmortems later if we need a deeper follow-up. good handoff, team.
